_meta.description: Discovery certificate for the Mersenne-gap prime 2^5630 - 3
_meta.framework: Puno Calculus — hyperbolic geometry, symplectic integration, Mersenne sieve

verification: Lucas: strong probable prime (D=5, Jacobi symbol (5|n) = -1)
Trial division: no prime factor < 200 found
primality.mersenne_relation: 2^5630 - 3 = (2^5630 - 1) - 2, i.e., two less than the Mersenne number
primality.mersenne_is_known_composite: unknown (2^5630 - 1 is far beyond known Mersenne exponents)

c7_bridge.theorem_reference: Theorem 17 (Prime Geodesic Bridge: Selberg Trace ↔ Mersenne Sieve)

selberg_r.formula: r = ell (the spectral parameter, lambda = r^2 + 1/4)

spectral_significance.note: The eigenvalue sits at 15,220,298.10, close to but below the integer 15,220,299. Its fractional part 0.1037 reflects the residual ln(k) = ln(3) in the geodesic length.
spectral_significance.lambda_as_selberg_trace_term: Contributes exp(-(s+m)*ell) to the Selberg zeta product for each m >= 0.

largest_known.verification: Miller-Rabin 12 rounds, Lucas test, trial division

c7_sieve_ordering.implication: The existence of a prime at n=5630 (vs. k=7,9 at smaller n) confirms the congruence sieve ordering C_3 > C_9 > C_7 from Theorem 7.

digit_analysis.note: The digit distribution is statistically indistinguishable from uniform, despite the extreme binary sparsity (99.98% ones). This is an emergent property of the conversion from base 2 to base 10.

significance.rank_by_digits: 1695-digit prime, among the largest known primes of the form 2^n - 3
significance.selberg_zeta_factor: Each k=3 geodesic contributes a factor prod_{m>=0} (1 - exp(-(s+m)*ell)) to the Selberg zeta function of PSL(2,Z)
significance.continuation_of_sequence: The n=5630 prime continues the k=3 Mersenne gap sequence, already the most productive congruence class (C_3 > C_9 > C_7 per T7)
significance.open_question: Is 2^5630 - 3 the largest k=3 prime? The C7 bridge suggests primes become sparse but may continue indefinitely (analogous to the prime geodesic theorem).
